payload.rationale: I estimate a 25% chance that NASA GISS’s reported unsmoothed 2026 Land-Ocean Temperature Index exceeds both 1.28°C and its reported 2025 value. This is a broad background-based judgment, not an estimate informed by observed 2026 temperatures. Established long-term warming makes further annual records plausible, but year-to-year variability, including ENSO effects, means warming does not produce a record every year. The two strict thresholds also make this narrower than simply forecasting another very warm year; a reported value equal to either threshold would not qualify. No supplied evidence establishes the 2025 value or 2026 temperatures through the September cutoff, so I retain substantial uncertainty rather than infer the missing observations. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that cooler ocean conditions or other natural variability could keep 2026 below 1.28°C, or 2025 could supply a higher hurdle. The strongest reason it could be too low is that persistent exceptional ocean warmth, continued underlying warming, or a strong warming-phase ENSO influence could make a new record substantially more likely.
limitations: No outside evidence records were supplied.
The NASA GISS 2025 value and 2026 monthly observations are unavailable here; these would be central to a September forecast.
Current ENSO conditions and other climate forcings are not established by the supplied information.
Settlement depends on NASA GISS’s specified unsmoothed index and reported precision, not another dataset or temperature-baseline convention.
